strengths: Rigorous mathematical framework with novel measure-based concentration bounds for softmax attention, carefully handling technical challenges like heavy-tailed exponential terms
Original training stability result (Theorem 4.3) extending concentration along entire gradient flow trajectories, enabling finite-prompt analysis via infinite-prompt limits
Extends anisotropic covariate results beyond prior work (Chen et al. 2024's isotropic-only restriction), demonstrating generality of approach
Elegant unified framework connecting finite and infinite prompt regimes, enabling transfer of linear attention theoretical results to softmax setting
Complete and detailed proofs with clear exposition of proof techniques
weaknesses: Extremely restrictive assumptions severely limit applicability: requires centered Gaussian inputs, sub-Gaussianity with E[σ_μ^12] < ∞, exponential σ-dependence makes bounds loose for realistic data distributions
Single-layer setting far from practice—unclear how insights transfer to multi-layer transformers used in modern LLMs; practical relevance questionable

Theoretical results contradict stated motivation: paper claims softmax outperforms linear attention empirically, but theory shows equivalence at infinite-prompt limit; Figure 2 shows linear outperforms softmax at finite L
Weak training dynamics guarantees: Theorem 4.3 only bounds limiting risk, not convergence of trajectories; requires appropriately chosen sequences T(L); no explicit convergence rates provided

Severely limited experiments: only synthetic in-context linear regression (toy problem), small dimensions (d=5), moderate prompt lengths (L≤1000), no real data or practical validation demonstrating utility beyond theory confirmation
Concentration bounds with σ^6 ln(L)/L^{c₂/σ²} rate have unclear tightness; 'large-prompt regime' never formally defined with respect to L and σ
Limited novelty relative to concurrent work: heavily builds on Castin et al. 2025 (Lemma 2.1), Bohbot et al. 2025 (similar concentration), Chen et al. 2024 (with incremental covariate generalization)

Multi-level theoretical results from concentration bounds to training dynamics to concrete application
Comprehensive proofs with detailed appendix (38 pages) demonstrating technical competence
Validates theoretical predictions with experiments on concentration and parameter convergence

Rigorous non-asymptotic concentration bounds (Propositions 3.1 and 3.4) quantifying convergence rates, with careful handling of heavy-tailed terms like exp(z_k^T U z)
Extends concentration results to entire training trajectories (Theorem 4.3) in general in-context learning settings, bridging asymptotic and practical regimes
Broader applicability than concurrent work (e.g., Chen et al. 2024) by handling anisotropic Gaussian covariates with more modular proof strategy
Proves Bayes optimality of softmax attention in in-context linear regression (Theorem 5.2), showing it recovers the optimal solution
Technically sophisticated proofs addressing subtle issues (e.g., autocorrelation in Remark 3.2, case-based analysis for different norm regimes)
Clear presentation with well-motivated problem setup and logical flow from concentration bounds to training dynamics to applications
Experimental validation on both isotropic and anisotropic data confirming theoretical predictions

Single-layer analysis only—modern LLMs use many layers, and multi-layer extensions are unclear and potentially non-trivial
